claim: Direct subgroup sampling reduces MSE of predicted-class-0 risk versus a globally random budget.
Risk-score-stratified acquisition within a predicted class improves subgroup risk estimation versus subgroup SRS.
Acquiring labels inside a rare predicted class estimates its risk more accurately than the prelabel score mean.
Subgroup stratification reduces risk estimation error relative to spending same global budget without group targeting.
Within-subgroup SRS is at least as efficient as uncertainty-stratified sampling for small subgroup counts.
